div.head: VIII Atr 36
div.ab: And wise wæran worldwitan þe to godcundan rihtlagan woroldlaga settan, folc to steore, ⁊ Criste ⁊ cyninge gerehtan þa bote þar man swa scolde manega for neode gewildan to rihte.

And secular councillors showed wisdom in appointing civil laws to uphold the privileges of religion, for the governance of the people, and in assigning the compensation to Christ and the king, so that thereby many are forced of necessity to submit to justice.

Und weise waren die Staatsregenten, welche zu geistlichen Rechtsgesetzen staatliche Gesetze aufstellten, dem Volke zur Zucht, und Christo und dem König den Bussertrag zusprachen, wofern viele so durch Zwang zum Recht gezwungen werden mussten.

And wise were the secular councillors who added secular laws to the laws of God, for the discipline of the people, and assigned the compensation to Christ and the king, so that many might thus be forced to right by compulsion.
div.note: D gives c. 36 a second time (after Wulfstan ed. Napier p. 169). Liebermann corrects ‘gerihtan’ to ‘gerehtan’ from that second copy. Liebermann compares EGu Prol. and VIII Atr 15.
